chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from someone who reported it, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The believer has strength in religion, and firmness in gentleness, and faith in conviction, and eagerness in jurisprudence, and activity in guidance, and righteousness in uprightness, and knowledge in forbearance, and cleverness in gentleness, and generosity in truth, and moderation in wealth, and composure in poverty, and pardoning in power, and obedience to Allah in sincerity, and restraint in lust, and piety in desire, and eagerness in jihad, and prayer in busyness, and patience in hardship, and dignified in turmoil, and patient in difficulties, and grateful in prosperity.

And he does not backbite, nor is he arrogant, nor does he cut off kinship, and he is not weak, nor harsh, nor rough, nor does his sight precede him, nor does his belly disgrace him, nor does his private part overcome him, nor does he envy people. He is reproached but does not reproach, and he is not extravagant. He helps the oppressed, and he is merciful to the poor. His soul is tired from him, but people are at rest from him. He does not desire the honor of the world, nor does he grieve over its disgrace.

People have a concern upon which they have turned, and for him there is a concern that occupies him. No deficiency is seen in his judgment, nor weakness in his opinion, nor waste in his religion. He guides the one who consults him, and assists the one who assists him, and shields from vulgarity and ignorance.
ai.seo_question: What are the key signs and characteristics of a true believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) outlines the 'signs of the believer' through a series of balanced virtues, reflecting the Shia concept of *Tawazun* (equilibrium) between spiritual rigor and social grace. It emphasizes that true faith manifests not only in private piety but also in reliable judgment (*Hukm*) and intellectual soundness (*Ra'y*), serving as a practical guide for communal leadership. The text underscores the believer's role as a stabilizing force who remains composed in adversity and generous in prosperity, aligning with the ideal of the *Imam al-Adl* (Just Leader) on an individual level.
